source.check: deemed re-elected (no nomination; the sitting member was returned automatically); sat as a member in the council-meeting report of the Lisburn Standard, 1936-06-12, p. 8 (monthly meeting of Tuesday 9 June 1936, 'attending who were not at the annual meeting') (round 2, 7 Nov 2026)

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received on 7 May 1936. One new member, Mr. William Porter, was returned for Ballykeel; in the other nine divisions (Ballymacbrennan, Ballyskeagh, Blaris, Breda, Carryduff, Dromara, Drumbo, Edenderry, Hillsborough) the sitting members were automatically returned, five of whom are recorded from Lisburn Standard reports of the June and July 1936 meetings (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026). Polling in County Down was fixed for 28 May 1936. One place-name in the list is John Martin's address, not a division; he is the member for Anahilt. Filed on 1936-06-04, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Down that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1936-05-28 (verification 5 Nov 2026). Ballyskeagh (A. A. Gillespie, co-opted for it in March 1931) is added from the meeting of 9 June 1936 (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). division from his co-option for Ballyskeagh in March 1931 'in the room of Mr. Robert Simpson, as the representative for Ballyskeagh' (Lisburn Standard, 13 March 1931, p. 9, which prints the name 'Albert Brown'; the council welcomed 'Mr. Albert Gillespie, recently co-opted' the next month, Lisburn Standard, 24 April 1931, p. 3, and the 1939 list names 'Albert A. Gillespie' for Ballyskeagh); the meeting report cited names the member as sitting early in the term. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
